title: Upper bound on fibre dimension on a neighbourhood
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $S$ a finite type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be prime and $\mathfrak p$ its inverse image in $R$. Write $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ for their residue fields [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$, the map sending $s\otimes a$ to $\bar s\bar a$. Suppose the dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ at $\mathfrak Q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is the integer $d\ge0$. Then there exists $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that, for every prime $\mathfrak p'\subset R$, if $S_g\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')\ne0$, its spectrum has Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$. Here $S_g$ denotes localization at the powers of $g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs), in the principal-open fibre-bound form explicitly used in Tag 00ST (lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection), proof part (3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-bounded-open-upstairs] to $R\to S$, $\mathfrak q$ and $d$. Its definition of relative dimension is precisely the dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ at the kernel specified in our statement. It gives an open neighbourhood $V$ of $\mathfrak q$ such that every $\mathfrak q'\in V$ has fibre dimension at most $d$. By part (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], choose $g\in S$ with $\mathfrak q\in D(g)\subseteq V$. Thus $g\notin\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs); the principal-open choice in Tag 00ST (lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection), proof (3)

proof.text: Fix any prime $\mathfrak p'\subset R$. Set $F'=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, $\bar g=g\otimes1$ and $H=S_g\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-localization-away-base-change], $H\cong F'_{\bar g}$, compatibly with $s\otimes a\mapsto (s/1)\otimes a$. By part (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], $\operatorname{Spec}H$ is therefore homeomorphic to the open subspace $O=D(\bar g)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}F'$. A ring isomorphism induces inverse continuous spectrum maps by [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Algebra, Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), 00DL (lemma-tensor-product-localization) and 00E4 (lemma-standard-open), spelling out the fibres of the principal localization in 00ST (3)

proof.text: For any $\mathfrak Q'\in O$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] identifies its inverse image $\mathfrak q'\subset S$ as a prime lying over $\mathfrak p'$, with $\mathfrak Q'$ equal to the kernel of $F'\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$. As $\bar g\notin\mathfrak Q'$, one has $g\notin\mathfrak q'$, so $\mathfrak q'\in D(g)\subseteq V$. Step 1 gives $\dim_{\mathfrak Q'}\operatorname{Spec}F'\le d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace], $\dim_{\mathfrak Q'}O=\dim_{\mathfrak Q'}\operatorname{Spec}F'\le d$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram); Topology Definition 0055 (definition-Krull) and its following remark

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] to $O$. Step 3 bounds every term of the supremum by $d$, hence $\dim O\le d$. The homeomorphism of Step 2 preserves Krull dimension: it takes irreducible closed subsets to irreducible closed subsets and its inverse does the same, preserving strict inclusions and hence the lengths of all chains in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Therefore $\dim\operatorname{Spec}H=\dim O\le d$. This proves the requested bound whenever $H\ne0$. If $O$ is empty, its dimension and the supremum over its points are both $-\infty$, so no nonemptiness assumption was needed for the inequality.
